page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8a.xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 9T24 processor running at 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 4 physical cores and 1.0 thread per core, providing dedicated compute resources without hyperthreading. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The instance includes no local storage, requiring external network-attached storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals distinct performance characteristics for this hardware profile. The AMD EPYC processor delivers strong single-core CPU performance, scoring 3071.48 in stress-ng single-core tests, which places it in the top 25%. However, multi-core scaling is more moderate, with stress-ng multi-core performance and PassMark CPU scores falling into the average range. Memory performance is mixed; while large-block memory write bandwidth and PassMark memory scores are average, read-only memory bandwidth for both small and large blocks is weak, falling into the bottom 25%. Similarly, database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput are positioned in the lower performance tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.r8a.xlarge offers a dense memory allocation relative to its compute footprint, making it suitable for memory-bound workloads that do not require high-speed local storage or extreme memory read bandwidth. The presence of advanced CPU instruction sets, such as AVX-512 and vector neural network instructions (VNNI), adds value for specialized vector processing. This instance is best suited for workloads such as caching layers, moderate database deployments, memory-intensive enterprise applications, and general-purpose tasks requiring a high RAM-to-vCPU ratio.
